body:
miscommunication is something that plagues me constantly.



in my 3rd game of the DPC Normal, i played against Erik Petersen.  in my TR i addressed my disappointment in how long our game took.  Erik and i resolved that problem soon after our game.  i was not angry at him, for sometimes games do take time, but i was just angry at timing out.  it’s not his fault.  i hold no grudge.  i haven’t thought about since the DPC until it was brought to my attention tonight.



retracting what i stated (as the truth and as what i felt to be true during the game) would be inaccurate, or so i believe.



forgetting to include in my report that Erik and i communicated to each other post-match about my disappointment was my mistake.  the issue was resolved then and there, and i thank him for not allowing that wound to fester.



sometimes (okay...quite often) i’m a pretty bad sport if i feel i didn’t get a good game out of it.



hey, i apologize.  any comments?



(i’m probably leaving something out, but try not to crucify me for it....that’s the miscommunication talking again)
title: Miscommunication
author: Geoff Snider
summary: A short follow-up note by Geoff Snider to his report [[Geoff Snider Geoff's DPC Main Event (tournament report)]] on the [[2001 Normal DPC]]: he says he and his round-3 opponent [[Erik Petersen]] resolved his complaint about their slow, timed-out game right after the match, and apologizes for leaving that out of the report.
notes: Follow-up note (posted 7 March 2001), not a game report; event = the report's event [[2001 Normal DPC]] (existing hub), author_played true. The round-3 game against Erik Petersen (timed win, +22) is already recorded from d1797, so no games here.
Hub facts copied from the live hub; players left null (86 already on the hub).
